raw_case_text:
On August 2007 a 43-year-old patient presented with the sudden onset of cholestatic jaundice and the radiologic detection of two pancreatic masses, diffuse lymphadenopathy, and hepatomegaly. To exclude the presence of a lymphoma, the patient underwent exploratory laparotomy. A biopsy of liver and of a lymph node at the level of hepatic hilum and cholecystectomy were performed. Biopsy of pancreatic mass was attended but, for technical reasons, not successful. Histology showed the presence of chronic cholecystitis with hypertrophic reactive lymphadenitis, fibrosis of the cystic duct with strong intramural inflammatory infiltrate, signs of portal fibrosis, and cholestasis in the absence of alterations of the biliary tract. Consequently, a bile duct-duodenal anastomosis was packed in absence of a conclusive diagnosis.
On March 2008, the patient presented a complex clinical picture including an interstitial pneumonitis by Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Chlamydia pneumoniae, Epstein Barr and cytomegalovirus infections, tubulointerstitial nephritis, severe lymphopenia, and marked reduction of CD4 (214 cells/muL, Tables 1 and 2). CT scan showed the presence of three pulmonary nodules (<1 cm), diffuse lymph node enlargement, and enlarged kidneys and spleen. Laboratory showed increased levels of ESR and CRP, hypergammaglobulinemia, positive reuma test and Waaler Rose tests, presence of serum and urinary kappa and lambda light chains, increased beta2 microglobulin, and circulating C1q immunocomplexes. ANA, anti-mitochondrial antibody, anti-bile canaliculi, anti-liver kidney mouse, liver western blot, anti-smooth muscle, pANCA, cANCA, anti-thyroglobulin, and anti-peroxidase were negative. Tests for leishmaniasis, toxoplasma, and HIV were also negative. The bone marrow aspirate excluded lymphoproliferative and parasitic disorders. Renal biopsy showed a tubulointerstitial nephritis with diffuse infiltrate of lymphocytes and plasma cells. Arteries and arterioles were undamaged. Immunohistochemistry revealed the presence of CD20, CD3, and CD68. Immunostaining for kappa and lambda light chains documented a polytypic plasma cells population. Direct immunofluorescence was negative for IgA, IgG, IgM, C3, C1q, fibrinogen, kappa, and lambda light chains. Subject was treated with glucocorticoids with improvement of the symptoms and lymphopenia.
Three years later, a reduction of the number of the CD4 lymphocytes was once again reported (146/muL, CD4/CD8 ratio equal to 0.8) in conjunction with the onset of fatigue, weight loss, night sweats, arthralgia, hemorrhagic rhinitis, multiple caries, and consequent extraction of 10 teeth. After the exclusion of HIV and malignancies (biopsy of an inguinal lymph node, bone marrow biopsy, and PET), an idiopathic CD4 lymphocytopenia was diagnosed. Nevertheless, only a part of the signs was explained by CD4 lymphocytopenia.
On January 2014, there was the first visit to our outpatient clinic for worsening renal function, hypocomplementemia, and polyclonal increase of IgG. CD4 lymphocytes were in the normal range.
The medical history of obstructive jaundice pancreatic mass and interstitial nephritis, together with a marked elevation of IgG4, was suggestive of a IgG4-related disease. At the time of our observation, ultrasound examinations showed hepatomegaly, increased volume of the kidneys with a mild dilatation of chalices and renal pelvis without signs of urinary tract obstructions, and bilateral enlargement of the submandibular glands. IgG4 were mildly elevated (185 mg/dL), ANA were negatives, and CD4 were in the normal range.
After 3 months of prednisone 50 mg/day, we observed an improvement of the renal function paired with a reduction of inflammation, IgG, and kidneys volume and the disappearance of the dilatation of chalices and renal pelvis.
At the time of the submission of the present case report, the patient, treated with prednisone 5 mg/day, is in remission with stable GFR and normalization of IgG4 and CD4 lymphocytes.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 43-year-old patient presented in August 2007 with sudden-onset cholestatic jaundice and pancreatic masses, followed in 2008 and 2011 by interstitial pneumonitis, tubulointerstitial nephritis, fatigue, weight loss, night sweats, arthralgia, and CD4 lymphocytopenia, and in January 2014 by worsening renal function and bilateral submandibular gland swelling.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: In August 2007, the patient developed obstructive jaundice with two pancreatic masses, hepatomegaly, and lymphadenopathy managed by cholecystectomy and biliary-duodenal anastomosis after biopsies excluded lymphoma. In March 2008, the patient developed interstitial pneumonitis, tubulointerstitial nephritis, and CD4 lymphopenia (214 cells/uL) that improved with glucocorticoids; in 2011, CD4 count dropped to 146 cells/uL with constitutional symptoms, hemorrhagic rhinitis, and severe dental caries; and in January 2014, the patient presented to our clinic with worsening renal function, bilateral submandibular gland enlargement, and hypergammaglobulinemia.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of biliary-duodenal anastomosis (2007), Mycoplasma/Chlamydia interstitial pneumonitis, EBV and CMV infections, and prior diagnosis of idiopathic CD4 lymphocytopenia (2011).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for prior obstructive jaundice, fatigue, weight loss, night sweats, arthralgia, hemorrhagic rhinitis, dental loss (10 teeth), and submandibular swelling.

objective.physical_examination: Hepatomegaly and bilateral submandibular gland enlargement.
objective.routine_investigations: Labs showed elevated ESR and CRP, polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia with elevated serum IgG4 (185 mg/dL), hypocomplementemia, worsening renal function, positive rheumatoid factor and Waaler-Rose tests, elevated beta2-microglobulin, and circulating C1q immune complexes. Autoantibodies (ANA, AMA, ASMA, LKM, pANCA, cANCA, anti-thyroid) and infectious tests for Leishmania, Toxoplasma, and HIV were negative. Ultrasound in January 2014 showed hepatomegaly, bilaterally enlarged kidneys with mild pelvicalyceal ectasia without obstruction, and bilateral submandibular gland enlargement.
objective.advanced_workup: CD4+ T-lymphocyte count was 214 cells/uL in 2008, 146 cells/uL (CD4/CD8 ratio 0.8) in 2011, and normal in January 2014. Chest/abdominal CT (2008) showed three subcentimeter pulmonary nodules, diffuse lymphadenopathy, splenomegaly, and nephromegaly. Bone marrow aspirate/biopsy, inguinal lymph node biopsy, and PET scan excluded lymphoma and parasitic infection; 2007 hepatic/hilar biopsies showed portal fibrosis, cholestasis, and fibrosing cholecystitis; 2008 renal biopsy demonstrated lymphoplasmacytic tubulointerstitial nephritis (CD20+, CD3+, CD68+, polytypic kappa/lambda, negative immunofluorescence).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Lymphoma, visceral leishmaniasis, HIV, and systemic lupus/vasculitis were excluded; integrating the history of autoimmune pancreatitis-like masses, sclerosing cholangitis/cholecystitis, sialadenitis, polytypic lymphoplasmacytic tubulointerstitial nephritis, hypocomplementemia, and elevated serum IgG4 (185 mg/dL) established a unifying diagnosis of IgG4-related disease (with secondary transient CD4 lymphocytopenia). Oral prednisone (50 mg/day for 3 months, tapered to 5 mg/day maintenance) normalized renal function, serum IgG/IgG4, and CD4 counts and resolved the nephromegaly and pelvicalyceal ectasia.
